This is the service homeowners and property managers ask for most. Air Duct Cleaning in North Clairemont, CA removes built up dust, lint, pet hair, and debris that collect in your supply and return lines. Clean ducts move air better and help keep filter changes from turning into a monthly chore.

How our duct cleaning process works

  • Inspection and plan
    • We check registers, returns, the air handler, and visible duct runs.
    • We look for leaks, kinks, and crushed sections that may need repair.
  • Home protection
    • Floor and register protection go down before we start.
  • HEPA negative air and agitation
    • We connect a powerful vacuum with HEPA filtration.
    • We use rotary brushes and air whips to loosen debris from duct walls.
  • Supply and return cleaning
    • Every register and return is addressed, including the ones over the hallway that nobody likes to reach.
  • Optional disinfecting and deodorizing
    • We can apply a safe fog treatment for Residential HVAC Air Duct Disinfecting or Commercial HVAC Air Duct Disinfecting, helpful after remodels or if you notice lingering odors.
  • Sealing options
    • If we find leaks, we can seal them, which helps keep dust out and comfort in.
  • Test and tidy
    • We verify airflow, reattach registers, and clean up.

Most single family homes in the 92117 area take a few hours. Larger homes near Clairemont Drive or multi unit properties near Clairemont Town Square may take longer. You will get a clear timeline before we begin.

How Often Should You Book Service

  • Air ducts
    • Every 3 to 5 years for most homes. Pets, heavy dust, or remodels may shorten that to every 2 to 3 years.
  • HVAC tune up

  • Filters
    • Standard 1 inch filters every 1 to 3 months. Larger media filters every 6 to 12 months.
  • Dryer vents

A Few Final Tips You Can Use Today

  • Check your filter
    • If you cannot see light through it, it is time to change it.
  • Look at supply vents
    • Dust streaks on the ceiling near vents can hint at dirty ducts or weak filters.
  • Listen for odd sounds
    • A rattling grille or whistling vent often means airflow imbalance or a loose connection.
  • Peek at the dryer vent
    • If the roof cap flap does not move when the dryer runs, you likely have a clog.
